content.title: About
content.content: McDouble is a double burger from McDonald’s, made of two beef patties, a slice of cheese, onions, pickles, mustard and ketchup, all sandwiched between two buns.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The McDouble was introduced in 1997 as a lower‑price alternative to the Double Cheeseburger.
It contains about 390 calories, making it less caloric than the classic Double Cheeseburger.
In some countries the burger can be served without onions upon request.
The McDouble is often featured in “2 for $X” promotions.
It is popular among students because of its price and size.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Two beef patties provide roughly 20 g of protein, essential for muscle repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Beef supplies heme iron, which is more readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: Calcium content
items.content: The cheese adds calcium, important for bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef and the bun provide B12 and niacin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Carbohydrates in the bun give a quick source of energy.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: Ketchup and pickles make the burger high in sodium, which can be an issue for hypertension.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Beef patties and cheese contain saturated fats, which should be limited in heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk allergy.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: The bun contains wheat, so the product is not suitable for a gluten‑free diet.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: McDouble is typically served in its standard packaging and can be eaten as a standalone snack or paired with fries and a drink. You can customize it with extra sauces or omit ingredients such as onions.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store a prepared McDouble in the refrigerator for no more than 24 hours. For longer storage, reheat in a microwave or oven to retain flavor and texture.
